independent_checks: Reconstructed all 490 pass chunks from the two gzip dumps. All 14 kernel GLIR anchors matched uniquely and exactly; TTGIR also matched in the corresponding invocation rather than assigning kernels by test order.
All 28 extracted MLIR snippets matched their declared raw byte ranges after exterior-whitespace stripping and final-newline addition; every declared snippet SHA256 matched.
All allocations, stores, and loads in the 14 post-allocation snippets were represented completely and consistently in the persisted summary.
All 14 tmem_size metadata values matched generated kernel metadata. Only select64-late, select32-late and chain64-late changed total TMEM capacity from 64 to 128 columns.
Fixed temporary intervals were [64,128), [64,96), and [64,128), respectively. The 128-column total capacity does not imply that the 32-column temporary itself uses 64 columns.
Code and summary correctly limit the evidence to static compiler IR and do not claim sampled hardware reads or writes.
limits: selected_source_value is matched using the distinctive 3/5 constants and independently verified reference values of this regression; selector expressions are not symbolically executed and no selected descriptor was dynamically sampled.
static_runtime_consistency_cases=16 includes passing controls. This is one upstream defect, not 16 distinct defects or a general detection-accuracy benchmark.

Pass attribution uses the contiguous serial dump region between two exactly matched GLIR anchors. It does not assume test-case compilation order, but it does not support interleaved concurrent compilation logs.
The hazard analyzer checks loads through arith.select. Direct-load controls are consistent with manual snippet inspection and numeric results, but the analyzer does not generally prove their safety.
